decisions.decision_value: Develop an original, trendy, and user-friendly infrared remote control
decisions.rationale: Initial project brief to create an original, trendy, and user-friendly remote control.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: we're supposed to develop a new remote control, that's both original, trendy and user-friendly.

decisions.decision_value: Selling price of 25 Euros, revenue target of 50 million Euros, and production cost cap at half the selling price (12.50 Euros)
decisions.semantic_target_quote: And the production cost should be the half of the selling price.

decisions.decision_value: Target users aged 16 to 40, controlling only one device (television) with no teletext and visible corporate identity
decisions.rationale: Management newsflash eliminated teletext, restricted control to the TV only, and targeted customers below 40.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: the basic new requirements of the management were no teletext, only for T_V_. Uh it should be designed for a use g uh group below forty,

decisions.decision_value: Include a top-mounted LCD screen to house all advanced configuration menus (audio, brightness/colour, channel programming)
decisions.rationale: Users under 40 are strongly interested in an LCD screen, and putting advanced settings in an LCD menu keeps the physical device simple.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: So it looks very simple and all the advanced features are hidden in the screen, uh with a clear menu.

decisions.decision_value: Build in speech recognition with a top-mounted microphone
decisions.rationale: Market research showed customers under 40 find speech recognition very interesting.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: above forty people are not so interested uh not so interested in a screen or speech recognition. Uh but below that age they uh they pretty much are. So I think we can build that in.

decisions.decision_value: 15 push-buttons with LED backlighting (power, 10 number keys, 4 directional volume/channel arrows, menu, okay, and back)
decisions.rationale: Separates basic channel/volume zapping buttons from LCD menu navigation buttons.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Yeah you have basically a button menu, which you can use directly, uh according to the old principle.

decisions.decision_value: Kinetic energy source (powered by shaking/moving the remote)
decisions.rationale: Long-lasting so users never buy batteries again, fun for young users, and pairs well with a bounce-resistant rubber case.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: But I really think that we should maybe uh think about the kinetic energy, where you have to move the thing to be able to use it.

decisions.decision_value: Double-curved (3D ergonomic hourglass/GameCube-like) case shape with non-flipping recessed LCD screen
decisions.rationale: Daring, fresh 3D curves appeal to young users; flipping screen mechanism was rejected because it could break when dropped or shaken for kinetic energy.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: well you know that we will have to go for the double curved 'cause it's daring and different from what we have now.

decisions.decision_value: Spongy rubber case material in bright primary fruit/vegetable colours with red LED push-buttons
decisions.rationale: Matches the spongy fruit-and-vegetable fashion trend for young consumers and protects the remote when dropped.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: I would definitely go for rubber 'cause it fits most in what people wanna see nowadays.

decisions.rationale: Required to support the LCD screen and audio/speech functions.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Yeah we need the the chip on print to be able to support the the screen and uh and f audio function.

decisions.rationale: Reflects the company brand Real Reaction and reuses the double-R corporate logo.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: I uh thought up a name for our product. Yeah. It's called uh the Real Remote.

decisions.decision_value: Switched from kinetic energy to a normal basic battery
decisions.rationale: Initial design cost ~26.50 Euros (more than double the 12.50 Euro limit); switching to a basic battery saved cost and avoided hand-dynamo power drain on the LCD screen.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Yeah but young people like that. So just do normal battery.

decisions.decision_value: Downgraded from double-curved to single-curved case (curved in front view, flat from the side)
decisions.rationale: Mandatory cost reduction to help bring the remote under the 12.50 Euro budget.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Well I guess i we'll have to go for single curve then. I mean we have to drop on everything.

decisions.decision_value: Dropped speech recognition (sample sensor/speaker, saving 4 Euros) while keeping the LCD screen
decisions.rationale: Although marketing data showed slightly higher popularity for speech recognition (81-91%) than the LCD screen (66-76%), the team dropped speech recognition because it was not yet integrated into their system, can be disturbed by room noise, and losing the LCD screen would destroy their entire menu-based concept and require many expensive physical buttons.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: We uh we we haven't really integrated this the speech into the system, so we can might as well s drop that.

decisions.decision_value: Kept the LCD screen and advanced chip-on-print as the core interface of the remote
decisions.rationale: The entire remote concept depended on the LCD screen to display all menus and channel/volume controls after physical buttons were removed to save money.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: We lose our whole concept. Uh so No we just We keep the L_C_D_.

decisions.decision_value: Switched case material from spongy rubber to hard plastic (free) while keeping special colours
decisions.rationale: Plastic is free (saving 2 Euros over rubber), and since kinetic energy was dropped the remote no longer needs to bounce; special colours were kept for visual appeal.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: Because we have to use the special colour anyway. You forgot that. So let's go for the plastic.

decisions.decision_value: Dropped all 15 push-buttons and replaced them with a single special-coloured integrated scroll-wheel push-button controlling all functions via the LCD screen
decisions.rationale: Replacing all individual push-buttons (including numbers 1-9, arrows, and power) with one integrated scroll-wheel push-button saved enough money to hit the 12.50 Euro budget while keeping the LCD screen and special colours.
decisions.semantic_target_quote: It s it saves us four Euros and it costs us two and a half. So let's see, we we drop the price by one and a half.

disagreements.positions: Speaker C proposed a laptop-style flip-up LCD screen to protect the display from scratches and hide advanced buttons underneath, whereas Speakers B and D argued a flipping hinge would easily break if dropped or shaken for kinetic energy.
disagreements.semantic_target_quote: But if you if you If you drop it it it just breaks. And it has to be very strong because of the.

disagreements.positions: Speaker C noted that speech recognition could replace many buttons and only required a regular chip (6 Euros total), and Speaker D found that speech recognition was actually more popular (81-91%) than an LCD screen (66-76%), but Speakers A, B, and D insisted on dropping speech recognition and keeping the LCD screen because their entire design was built around the screen and speech recognition can be disturbed by noise.
disagreements.semantic_target_quote: There are more people who like speech recognition than an L_C_D_ screen.

disagreements.positions: To stay under the 12.50 Euro budget while keeping the LCD screen and special colours, the team replaced all 15 buttons with a single integrated scroll-wheel push-button; during evaluation Speakers C, D, and A admitted this made the remote very difficult to use (scoring 6 out of 7 on ease of use) since users must multi-click and scroll through menus even to change channels or volume.
disagreements.semantic_target_quote: No. The only e the only thing easy about it is that you don't have to move your fingers. 'Cause it has only one button.
